issues.legal_issue: A competent authority must decide objections to a proposed land acquisition after hearing the objectors by making a reasoned order and communicating it to them.
material_facts: The landowners filed written objections and later received a personal hearing, after which they submitted further written objections.
No decision allowing or disallowing the objections was passed after the hearing or communicated to the landowners.
The authority relied on an earlier letter issued before the hearing and on internal file notings recording rejection of the objections; it also stated that no order had been passed after the hearing.
issues.conclusion: The mandatory objection procedure was not complied with. The pre-hearing letter was not a valid decision, and the internal file notings did not constitute an order deciding the objections.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20D(2) of the Railways Act, 1989 requires the competent authority, after hearing the objections and making any necessary further inquiry, to allow or disallow them by order. The objection right is a substantive and valuable safeguard, analogous to the right under Section 5-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and must not be reduced to a formality. A quasi-judicial authority must apply its mind and give a reasoned decision; internal file notings are not an effective order unless finalized and communicated. The Court relied on Union of India v. Shivraj; Hindustan Petroleum Corpn. Ltd. v. Darius Shapur Chenai; Laxmi Devi v. State of Bihar; Raghbir Singh Sehrawat v. State of Haryana; Kranti Associates (P) Ltd. v. Masood Ahmed Khan; Bachhittar Singh v. State of Punjab; Shanti Sports Club v. Union of India; and Sethi Auto Service Station v. DDA. It also applied the principle that when a statute prescribes how an act must be done, it must be done in that manner, and strictly construed the expropriatory procedure.

rule.if: acquisition_objection_appeal and written_objections_submitted and hearing_granted and not post_hearing_reasoned_order and not decision_communicated

predicates.acquisition_objection_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a land acquisition on the basis of how objections to the proposed acquisition were handled.
predicates.written_objections_submitted: Interested landowners submitted written objections to the proposed acquisition.
predicates.hearing_granted: The competent authority gave the objectors an opportunity to be heard.
predicates.post_hearing_reasoned_order: After the hearing, the competent authority made a reasoned decision allowing or disallowing the objections.
predicates.decision_communicated: The competent authority communicated its decision to the objectors.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-objection appeal involves written objections and a hearing but no reasoned post-hearing decision communicated to the objectors, the objections have not been lawfully disposed of.

issues.legal_issue: A procedural failure in an acquisition objection process does not require the entire acquisition to be set aside where exceptional circumstances make compensation to the affected challengers an appropriate remedy.
material_facts: The procedural failure concerned the landowners' challenge to a limited portion of a much longer public railway project.
Most of the remaining project stretch had been acquired, and substantial construction work had been completed or was underway.
The landowners did not allege mala fides and, through counsel, stated that they would be satisfied with compensation assessed at the current market value.
The remaining landowners had accepted the awarded compensation and had not challenged the acquisition before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to set aside the entire acquisition and confined relief to the appellants by directing compensation assessed on the basis of the land's current market value.
issues.legal_principle: Although the absence of a valid decision on objections invalidates subsequent steps in the acquisition as to the affected challenge, the remedy may be moulded to balance the affected owners' rights against a larger public purpose where the project is substantially advanced and setting aside the acquisition would not serve that purpose. The Court relied on Savitri Devi v. State of U.P. for the use of equitable, practical relief in light of developments on the ground, and directed current-market-value compensation assessed with reference to Section 20G of the Railways Act, 1989. The relief was confined to the challengers and was not made a precedent for other landowners who had not challenged the acquisition.

rule.if: acquisition_challenge_appeal and objections_not_lawfully_disposed and limited_land_segment_challenged and major_public_project_substantially_advanced and not mala_fides_alleged and claimants_accept_current_value_compensation

predicates.acquisition_challenge_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a land acquisition for a public project.
predicates.objections_not_lawfully_disposed: The competent authority failed to lawfully decide the objectors' objections after hearing them.
predicates.limited_land_segment_challenged: The challenge concerns only a limited portion of the land required for the larger project.
predicates.major_public_project_substantially_advan: A substantial part of the larger public project has been acquired or built, or construction is underway.
predicates.mala_fides_alleged: The challengers alleged that the acquisition process was driven by bad faith.
predicates.claimants_accept_current_value_compensat: The affected claimants indicated that compensation based on the land's current value would satisfy them.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge establishes defective objection disposal but concerns a limited segment of a substantially advanced public project, no bad faith is alleged, and the claimants accept current-value compensation, the claimants may receive compensation without the entire acquisition being set aside.
